scope.material_identity_warning: 13Cr-4Ni and ZG0Cr13Ni4Mo are a prior relationship, not a certificate-level identity

citation.title: Review on experimental investigation of sediment erosion in hydraulic turbines
citation.authors: Shrestha, Gurung, Chitrakar, Thapa, Neopane, Guo, Qian

evidence_uses.locator: page 3, discussion of Pelton bucket erosion regions
evidence_uses.claim: cutout regions, splitter and near-outlet regions are vulnerable zones
evidence_uses.allowed_use: region ordering prior for participant DEC face mapping
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: direct DEC face-wise truth or dimensional transfer

evidence_uses.claim: quartz and feldspar are described as hard sediment minerals with Mohs hardness approximately 7
evidence_uses.allowed_use: erodent hardness sensitivity range and test-material selection
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: substitute for measured PSD or mineralogy of the contest case

evidence_uses.claim: the review tabulates Finnie, Bitter, Liu et al. and Rai et al. relations for Pelton test or field contexts, including 04Cr13Ni5Mo runner-bucket and 13Cr-4Ni bucket entries
evidence_uses.allowed_use: pre-registered model-combination prior and sensitivity envelope
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: claim that the tabulated coefficients are independently calibrated for DEC

citation.title: Investigation of the Erosion Characteristics in the Distribution Parts of Pelton Turbine
citation.authors: L. Han, Y. Wang, G. F. Zhang, X. Z. Wei

evidence_uses.claim: the study compares spherical particles of 0.1, 0.5 and 1.0 mm and reports different following behavior and erosion patterns
evidence_uses.allowed_use: PSD scenario design and particle-transport sensitivity
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: transfer of its nozzle/needle erosion field to DEC bucket faces

evidence_uses.claim: the modeled condition includes an 80 m head and normalized nozzle opening 0.55
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: assertion that DEC has the same head or opening

citation.title: Hydro-Abrasive Erosion of Pelton Turbines
citation.author: Anant Kumar Rai
citation.institution: Alternate Hydro Energy Centre, Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee

evidence_uses.locator: pages iii-iv and thesis abstract summary
evidence_uses.claim: the work includes 13Cr-4Ni, 16Cr-5Ni and 16Cr-4Ni martensitic steels, bronze and coated variants, with optical 3D scanning and mass-loss measurements
evidence_uses.allowed_use: same-family material prior and independent measurement protocol design

evidence_uses.claim: the reported laboratory erosion velocities include 32.11, 28.97, 25.62 and 22.05 m/s
evidence_uses.allowed_use: velocity sensitivity envelope and pilot design check

evidence_uses.claim: the abstract summary reports coated-bucket curved-zone erosion depth around 0.4 percent of bucket thickness
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: direct DEC worn field or absolute depth truth

citation.title: Towards Multiscale Numerical Simulations of Pelton Turbine Erosion
citation.authors: Sebastian Leguizamon, Ebrahim Jahanbakhsh, Audrey Maertens, Siamak Alimirzazadeh, Francois Avellan

evidence_uses.claim: the presentation reports a prototype-scale case with B2 0.38 m, jet diameter 140 mm, jet velocity 28.5 m/s, real sediment size distribution and 1.46 million particles
evidence_uses.allowed_use: scale, particle-count and GPU validation planning prior
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: DEC boundary condition or material calibration

evidence_uses.claim: 13Cr-4Ni is characterized with Split-Hopkinson-bar data and a Johnson-Cook fit; the slide reports 4.1 percent standard deviation
evidence_uses.allowed_use: candidate constitutive-data provenance and uncertainty floor
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: formal FEM material card without the underlying raw test data

evidence_uses.locator: report discussion around printed pages 20-24 and 50-58
evidence_uses.claim: solid-particle erosion depends on particle velocity, attack angle, particle size, particle density and target hardness; the report discusses velocity and size effects for metallic targets
particle impact velocity must be measured or calculated carefully because erosion rate can have a high velocity exponent
evidence_uses.allowed_use: input-quality requirement for remote particle replay

citation.title: Solid Particle Erosion Modelling using CFD techniques
citation.author: Alok Sawant

evidence_uses.locator: printed contents pp. 94-120 and model-comparison chapter
evidence_uses.claim: the thesis implements and compares Oka, Grant-Tabakoff and related erosion-model formulations against CFD particle-impact quantities
evidence_uses.allowed_use: pre-registered model-comparison and numerical sensitivity workflow
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: transfer of its SS316 or elbow calibration to DEC

evidence_uses.claim: the thesis compares constant particle size with Rosin-Rammler particle-size distributions and varies velocity, impact angle and feed rate
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: claim that the selected PSD is the DEC sediment PSD

citation.title: Investigation of High-Cycle Fatigue Properties of Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing 13Cr4Ni Martensitic Stainless Steel
citation.authors: Guangfu Cheng, Haichao Li, Haiyan Dai, Hongming Gao, Jianchao Pang

evidence_uses.locator: pages 2 and 8, abstract and mechanical-properties discussion
evidence_uses.claim: the forged 13Cr4Ni specimen is reported at 280 HV and the WAAM specimen at 320 HV
evidence_uses.allowed_use: same-family hardness sensitivity interval for synthetic ZG0Cr13Ni4Mo reference

evidence_uses.claim: the forged specimen is reported at 685 MPa yield and 823 MPa ultimate tensile strength; the WAAM specimen is reported at 850 MPa yield and 927 MPa ultimate tensile strength
evidence_uses.allowed_use: exploratory material-envelope input and fatigue plausibility check

evidence_uses.claim: the study reports a 580 C x 2 h furnace heat-treatment step for the tested WAAM material
evidence_uses.forbidden_use: assumption about the DEC casting heat treatment
